gates.because: no threat row: an ADR citation in an authority document names its series, and a redirection page in docs/adr points at a tracked file.
no threat row: an ADR that is amended, superseded or replaced says so in its own header.
no threat row: the advisory waivers of docs/security/ADVISORY-WAIVER-POLICY.md follow that policy, with its clock-dependent expiry judged against the date.
no threat row: a crate's public API is compared to a git baseline with cargo-semver-checks, so a removed public item cannot ship without a version increment.
no threat row: every untracked or tracked file carries an ephemerality marker, and every marker has a condition that is not overdue.
no threat row: a pull request is judged only on the advisories its own lockfile change introduces, both sides being audited from the lockfile.
no threat row: the French and English normative specifications keep the same version, headings, code blocks and table row counts.
no threat row: the file has no header comment; from its code, it refuses forbidden commercial claims in the brand documents.
no threat row: every manifest resolves the Bun toolchain contract through the local or the pinned governance tooling.
no threat row: the file has no header comment; from its code, it checks that the running Bun is at least the minimumVersion of toolchains/bun.json.
no threat row: a manifest installed as a sha-pinned git-dep declares no specifier that resolves only inside this workspace.
no threat row: private identifiers and machine-local paths are absent from the public tree.
no threat row: every tracked file that is neither code nor Markdown is classified, so that no data file can loosen a guarded gate unseen.
no threat row: no source is unreachable from an entry point, no export is unreferenced, and no declared dependency is unused.
no threat row: the licence a publishable manifest declares matches the effective REUSE licence of its files.
no threat row: the repository's deny.toml is executed by cargo-deny against its committed Cargo graph, for bans, licenses and sources.
no threat row: doctrine exists only in the invariants register, every accepted ADR carries its owner-arbitration trace, and retired doctrine cannot resurface.
no threat row: long and unedited governance documents are listed for a human audit (migrate, archive or reconfirm); the command only lists.
no threat row: every allowEmpty call is nominatively listed in code, so that no gate silences itself without a reviewed entry.
no threat row: tracked source refuses a download handed to an interpreter, a permission opened to every account, an IPv4 connection target and a tolerated workflow failure without a reason.
no threat row: evicted content does not reappear in the tree, no tracked file names an evicted path, and every recoverable location resolves.
no threat row: heavy objects in a repository's history are listed with a recommendation, and project names that name a tool are reported; nothing is rewritten.
no threat row: identifiers that must not appear in the tree are found by the SHA-256 of their tokens, without the identifiers being written in readable form.
no threat row: every import specifier of a package respects its declared dependencies, and no specifier names a product package.
no threat row: the organisation's issue forms keep the required fields, labels and headings that the gates read.
no threat row: third-party JavaScript licences belong to the reviewed allowed list, and first-party licences are decided by resolved source.
no threat row: the K1 to K5 status table of the loop security kernel is the single source that every other status claim must match.
no threat row: each Rust crate reaches its mutation survivor threshold, and a run that generates zero mutant is a failure, never a pass.
no threat row: no Clever Cloud resource and no production claim appears in living surfaces before G4.
no threat row: the local-only apps do not import or call any network primitive, so user data never leaves the device.
no threat row: the objective files, the forbidden-statement scan and the vision corpus are each verified, and a scan that inspects no file fails.
no threat row: credentials carried under a non-issuer shape (hexadecimal or base64 values, literals in secret-named fields) are detected.
no threat row: the published tree carries no instance data about organisations or natural persons (invariant I-21).
no threat row: every pinned code citation names a commit, a path and lines that exist.
no threat row: every pull request declares whether its change can be walked back, names a second instrument for a one-way change, and declares its origin.
no threat row: the negatives a pull request declares about itself are not contradicted by its own diff.
no threat row: every criterion of an approved PRD is cited by a row of the work-package table, and a specification with no criterion fails.
no threat row: the declared shared source trees name no consuming product, under named patterns held in data.
no threat row: the fleet refusals register has its declared shape, and every refusal rests on public, pinned or dated evidence.
no threat row: the relative links, reference definitions and HTML links of tracked Markdown resolve to files and to heading anchors, offline.
no threat row: a branch supplied to a request is resolved from the repository, never written as a literal.
no threat row: retired tooling names are not reused as a workspace directory or as a package or crate name.
no threat row: repository names retired by the authority consolidation are not referenced operationally.

a pull request that mutates the human-touch surface (I-17: the registers and the ADRs) must point at a review artefact or at a dated owner-arbitration marker, so that no agent review stands for the human touch.
no threat row: a rule feedback ticket carries identifiers only, in its declared shape, so that no rule text or project description leaves the machine.
no threat row: no committed credential (cloud key, VCS or CI token, private key) appears in a living surface.
no threat row: every tracked shell script passes shellcheck at error severity.
no threat row: the file has no header comment; from its code, it refuses non-bun lockfiles and plain JavaScript sources in the tree, and fails if it read no file.
no threat row: the application specifications are locked in governance mode or in product-repository mode, and zero inspected specifications is a failure.
no threat row: the third-party exit register has its declared shape, and no exit exercise past its due date lacks a record.
no threat row: every I-xx cited in the declared security documents is a live register row, and a mention of a retired row is admitted only as declared in data.
no threat row: every tracked gate has exactly one coverage entry, and every covers identifier is a row of the threat model; the relevance of a covers is not judged.
no threat row: every threat of the STRIDE and LINDDUN section names an existing control or a residual, and the evidence the ledger names exists.
no threat row: the toolchain contract is satisfied through the local or the pinned governance tooling.
no threat row: a version, a date or a count written in a root document is derived by a named command, not typed by hand.
no threat row: every pull request names the work package it delivers, through a commit trailer, or an exemption class it verifies.
